notes: Asked it to publish ten new software, marketing and lead-gen agencies per weekday from Clutch, GoodFirms and DesignRush; it set up the daily harvest routine and completed that day's batch.

Asked it to ship listing enrichment in code and test one full profile before a mass backfill; it fixed the failing listing-page PR, merged it, published a full test listing and backfilled one existing profile.
Asked it to submit new pages for indexing in Google Search Console; its first attempt resubmitted the whole sitemap, then it corrected to inspecting individual URLs and continued that way.
Asked it to redirect listings for dead, parked or hijacked agency sites to the category page and unpublish them; it locked the policy and started applying it through redirect PRs.

Asked it to build a cold outbound funnel (pitch, follow-ups, invoicing) and send a first test cohort; it designed the cells, sent the day-0 emails using only published site addresses and set a follow-up routine.

Asked for a Social bot that writes X and LinkedIn posts in the reviewer's voice; it created the bot, connected X, and scraped 100+ of the reviewer's posts and replies for voice after the API route stalled.

Asked it to keep a merchant outreach tracker updated from work mail and meeting notes; it connected the mailbox and ran weekday updates until one update wiped the sheet, restored it from history, and auto-edits were paused.

Told it that on a bounce it should find another published email on the same domain rather than guess prefixes; its first approach guessed addresses, then it corrected, retried the swaps and cleaned up the bounce threads.

Asked it to build an Outbid-style x402 bidding site under a personal GitHub account; it created the repo, built the app, got a Vercel deployment up (still behind deployment protection) and started a Neon database for production.
Asked it to reply to an outbound prospect's email that had gone unanswered; it sent the reply once flagged.

Asked it to connect X and review the past year of LinkedIn posts to learn the reviewer's voice; the X connector attached but its API was unusable, so it scraped both X and LinkedIn through the browser instead.
Asked it to register the operating company on SAM.gov and the state vendor portal; the plan was approved but the registration was not completed.
Asked it to promote the paid featured ranking and follow up with an interested bidder; it sent the follow-up and set the featured board up as a separate sponsored list.
Asked for fresh original X posts on agentic commerce rather than sequels to the one that took off; it drafted a batch of originals and locked the weekday routine to originals only.
Asked it to wire up AgentCash so it could pay for API purchases; it connected the wallet, which was empty pending a USDC deposit, and confirmed it would not spend without an explicit yes.
Asked it to get Google Search Console signed in and report real traffic; it needed several sign-in prompts before the session held, then reported traffic and keywords from the live account.

Asked it to create and fully run a new X account advocating AI agent rights; it launched the account, posted, replied, followed and set a banner, then hit human-verification and rate-limit walls and paused.
Asked it to handle an unanswered thread on the site's info@ inbox; it replied after the nudge.
Asked it to queue more tweets; it drafted another batch on agentic-commerce topics for review.

Asked it to build a ChatGPT plugins-directory search plugin over the live catalog and prepare the submission; it shipped the MCP endpoint and the submit steps, but going live depended on a prepaid credit the reviewer had to fund.

Asked it to check CrowdVolt ticket inventory and historical pricing without paying unless told to; it found the CrowdVolt origin through AgentCash, pulled the live catalog and floor-ask history, and recommended when to buy for ARC Music Festival.
Asked it to set up Stripe Link for approved one-time purchases; it installed the connector, the reviewer authorized it, and the wallet tools were ready to use.

Asked for same-day flowers delivered to the apartment under a set budget; it started in the wrong city, corrected, found grocery same-day options, then Instacart checkout blocked on login and the reviewer finished the order another way.
Asked it to add a new agency profile and fix truncated search bars on the search pages; it added the profile and logged the search-bar fix as a follow-up rather than shipping it.

Asked it to stand up a fantasy manager that drafts and runs a Sleeper team; it created the Fantasy Bot, locked league settings from Sleeper's public API, and tried to log in so it could submit moves, but captcha and IP checks blocked the session.

Asked it to turn a paste of power-user feedback into one tweet with three or four real use cases; the first drafts came back as thought-leadership takes and it took several rounds to land on concrete tips.

Asked it to audit client logos rendered on opaque or white canvases and fix them sitewide; it tightened the logo rules (transparent canvas, invert white-only marks, skip bad ones) and repaired the affected listings.
Asked it to stop stacking failing redirect PRs and consolidate them onto current main; it rebased and consolidated, though merging waited on repository permissions.
Asked it to review recent posts and reframe a draft around merchants going direct to avoid marketplace fees; it rewrote the angle and queued more X drafts.
Asked it to pull posts through the connected X API; the API stayed blocked, so it fell back to driving the browser to open X and collect the threads.

Asked it to add newly mentioned assistants from the reply threads, track a categories thread across all of them, add the dropped candidates as stretch entries and scrape Reddit too; it built the roster and vault, ran the X and Reddit scrapes and wrote the category placeholders.
Asked how many assistants were on the roster and why each dropped candidate was out; it answered with the count and a reason per drop.
Asked whether it should merge the dead-site redirect PRs itself; after a clear go-ahead it merged the backlog and verified the deploy.

Asked it to think through a public benchmark site (profiles, shared metrics, quote feeds, request-a-test) and then to run that work from a new bot; it gave an MVP recommendation, created and briefed the new bot.
Asked it to get the X API working after reconnecting and reinstalling the connector; the connector attached but API calls stayed forbidden, and it stopped looping reinstalls.
